name: Unilateral Security Deposit Forfeiture
description: Unilateral total forfeiture of security deposit without genuine pre-estimate of damages.
patterns: deposit.*(?:shall not be refunded|non-refundable.*under any condition)
legalSource: Indian Contract Act, 1872 - Section 74 (Liquidated damages vs penalty stipulations; Kailash Nath Associates v. DDA, 2015 SC)
explanation: A clause providing for unconditional forfeiture of the entire deposit regardless of actual physical damages or unpaid rent acts as a punitive penalty stipulation, which is generally unenforceable under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act.
caveat: Landlords are entitled to deduct documented rent arrears or verified property repair costs, but absolute forfeiture without accounting requires legal scrutiny.

name: Unannounced Landlord Entry Without Prior Notice
description: Right of entry at any time without mandatory prior written or electronic notice.
patterns: enter.*(?:any time|without notice|at will|without prior permission)
legalSource: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 - Section 15 (Minimum 24-hour prior written/electronic notice mandatory before entry)
explanation: Unfettered right of landlord entry infringes on the tenant's right to quiet enjoyment and conflicts with statutory prior-notice standards.
caveat: Emergency entry during severe structural peril or environmental hazard is legally permissible; routine inspections require statutory advance notice.

name: Inadequate or Unreasonable Eviction Notice
description: Notice to vacate within unreasonably brief timeframes (e.g. 24 hours to 7 days).
legalSource: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 - Section 106 & Model Tenancy Act, 2021
explanation: A provision requiring the tenant to vacate within 24 to 48 hours without formal default remediation provides inadequate time to seek alternative housing and may be legally challenged.
caveat: Statutory notice periods vary based on whether eviction is for cause (e.g. persistent non-payment) or convenience.

name: One-Sided Notice Period Asymmetry
description: Notice period asymmetry where tenant is bound to excessive notice while owner may terminate abruptly.
legalSource: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 - Section 106 & Indian Contract Act Principles of Mutuality
explanation: Unequal termination notice terms create contractual imbalance favoring the property owner over the occupant.
caveat: Commercial and residential lease norms differ; mutual 30-day notice is standard practice for residential tenancies.

name: Unilateral or Discretionary Rent Escalation
description: Discretionary or uncalibrated rent hike without objective benchmark or mutually agreed cap.
patterns: rent.*(?:increased|escalated).*at the sole discretion of the landlord
legalSource: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 - Section 9 (Rent revision norms)
explanation: Discretionary rent increases allow arbitrary rent increases without mutual agreement during the tenancy term.
caveat: Standard annual escalation typically ranges between 5% and 10% in major urban centers.

name: Standard Mutual 30-Day Notice
legalSource: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 & Transfer of Property Act, 1882
explanation: A reciprocal notice clause where either party may terminate upon 30 days prior written notice adheres to statutory fair contracting standards.
caveat: Notice must be formally served in writing or electronic format according to agreement terms.
